dedupe_keys.name: nigeria high frequency crowdsourced prices hfcp of staple food commodities december 2024 to june 2025

description: This dataset holds daily retail, wholesale and farmgate prices of staple foods submitted by volunteers and trained enumerators from hundreds of markets in all 36 states of Nigeria and the Federal Capital Territory. It was curated by the National Bureau of Statistics under the Nigeria Food Price Tracking initiative with World Bank staff, and published in the World Bank Microdata Library in January 2026. The basket covers imported and local rice, white and yellow maize, garri, white and brown beans, soybeans, sorghum and yam. Submissions, mainly through mobile data platforms, pass automated validation and technical review, and outliers are removed in order of receipt so that each day shows the most reliable data available then. Each entry carries market location metadata for spatial analysis. Collection ran daily, with intraday submissions, from 1 December 2024 to 27 June 2025. The catalogue lists the data as open access, free to download. Caveats: volunteer coverage varies by market and day, and prices are self-reported by contributors. Simulation uses: high-frequency, geolocated staple prices for food market shock detection, market integration and affordability inputs to food supply resilience models. Related records: the earlier Food Price Crowdsourcing Africa data for Nigeria (data-nigeria-crowdsourced-food-prices-fpca) and WFP global food prices (data-wfp-global-food-prices) give other price series.
